title: UNIT 5: THERMAL PHYSICS
notes:
✓ Thermal physics → Deals with heat, temperature, internal energy, heat transfer, changes of state, thermal expansion and calorimetry.

✓ Heat → Energy transferred because of a temperature difference.

✓ Internal energy → Microscopic kinetic and potential energy contained within a system.

title: 5.1 HEAT, TEMPERATURE AND INTERNAL ENERGY
notes:
◆ HEAT
✓ Heat → Energy transferred from one system to another because of a temperature difference.

✓ Heat naturally flows → From higher temperature to lower temperature.

✓ Heat → Is not a substance stored inside an object; it is energy in transit.

◆ TEMPERATURE
✓ Temperature → Indicates the thermal state of a body and is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles.

◆ THERMAL EQUILIBRIUM
✓ Two objects are in thermal equilibrium → They have the same temperature.

✓ Thermal equilibrium → There is no net heat transfer between the objects.

◆ INTERNAL ENERGY
✓ Internal energy → Total microscopic energy of a system, including molecular kinetic energy and potential energy associated with molecular/atomic interactions, vibrations and chemical bonds.

✓ Increasing temperature → Generally increases internal energy.

✓ Change of state → Can also change internal energy.

◆ HEAT AND WORK
✓ Heat → Thermal energy transfer caused by temperature difference.

✓ Work → Mechanical energy transfer caused by a force acting through displacement.

✓ Heat and work → Are two different ways of transferring energy between systems.

✓ Heat and work → Can both change the internal energy of a system.

✓ Heat ≠ Temperature ≠ Internal energy.

✓ Temperature → Describes thermal condition.
✓ Heat → Is energy transferred.
✓ Internal energy → Is energy contained microscopically within the system.

title: 5.2 HEAT TRANSFER MECHANISMS
notes:
✓ Heat → Can be transferred mainly by conduction, convection and radiation.

◆ CONDUCTION
✓ Conduction → Heat transfer through collisions and interactions between neighboring particles without bulk movement of the material.

✓ Best associated with → Solids, especially metals.

✓ Heat flows → From the hotter region toward the colder region.

✓ Conduction rate for a uniform material:
P = Q/t = kAΔT/L

✓ k → Thermal conductivity.
✓ A → Cross-sectional area.
✓ ΔT → Temperature difference.
✓ L → Distance through which heat travels.

✓ High k → Good thermal conductor.
✓ Low k → Good thermal insulator.

◆ CONVECTION
✓ Convection → Heat transfer caused by the bulk movement of a fluid.

✓ It occurs in → Liquids and gases.

✓ Warm fluid → Becomes less dense and tends to rise.

✓ Cooler, denser fluid → Tends to sink → Producing convection currents.

◆ RADIATION
✓ Radiation → Transfers energy by electromagnetic waves and does not require a material medium.

✓ Thermal radiation → Can travel through vacuum.

✓ Examples → Energy from the Sun reaching Earth and heat felt from a fire.

◆ THERMAL INSULATORS
✓ Thermal insulators → Materials that reduce heat transfer.

✓ Aerogel → An example of an extremely effective thermal insulator.

◆ QUICK COMPARISON
✓ Conduction → Particle interactions.
✓ Convection → Bulk fluid movement.
✓ Radiation → Electromagnetic waves; no medium required.

title: 5.3 HEAT CAPACITY, SPECIFIC HEAT AND CHANGE OF STATE
notes:
◆ HEAT CAPACITY
✓ Heat capacity → Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of an object by 1°C or 1 K.

✓ C = Q/ΔT

✓ Therefore:
Q = CΔT

✓ SI unit → J/K.

◆ SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY
✓ Specific heat capacity → Heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by 1°C or 1 K.

✓ c = C/m

✓ Q = mcΔT

✓ Unit → J/(kg·K) or J/(kg·°C).

◆ HIGH VS LOW SPECIFIC HEAT
✓ High specific heat → Requires more energy for the same temperature increase.

✓ Low specific heat → Temperature changes more easily for the same heat supplied.

✓ Water → Has a high specific heat capacity, making oceans important heat reservoirs and helping moderate climate.

◆ CHANGE OF STATE
✓ Matter can change between:
Solid ⇄ Liquid ⇄ Gas

✓ Melting → Solid → Liquid.
✓ Freezing → Liquid → Solid.
✓ Vaporization → Liquid → Gas.
✓ Condensation → Gas → Liquid.
✓ Sublimation → Solid → Gas.
✓ Deposition → Gas → Solid.

✓ During a phase change → Energy is transferred without changing the temperature of the substance while the phase change occurs.

◆ LATENT HEAT
✓ Latent heat → Energy absorbed or released during a change of state without a temperature change.

✓ Q = mL

✓ L → Specific latent heat.

✓ Unit → J/kg.

◆ SPECIFIC LATENT HEAT OF FUSION
✓ Lf → Heat required per unit mass to change a solid into a liquid at its melting point without temperature change.

✓ Q = mLf

◆ SPECIFIC LATENT HEAT OF VAPORIZATION
✓ Lv → Heat required per unit mass to change a liquid into a gas at its boiling point without temperature change.

✓ Q = mLv

✓ Key idea → Temperature changes → Q = mcΔT.

✓ Phase changes → Q = mL.

✓ The two equations → Should not be confused.

title: 5.4 THERMAL EXPANSION
notes:
✓ Thermal expansion → Change in size of matter caused by a change in temperature.

◆ EXPANSION OF SOLIDS
✓ Solids can undergo:

◆ Linear expansion → Change in length.

◆ Surface/area expansion → Change in area.

◆ Volume/cubic expansion → Change in volume.

◆ LINEAR EXPANSION
✓ ΔL = αL₀ΔT

✓ L = L₀(1 + αΔT)

✓ α → Coefficient of linear expansion.

✓ Unit of α → K⁻¹ or °C⁻¹.

◆ AREA EXPANSION
✓ ΔA = βA₀ΔT

✓ β ≈ 2α

✓ A = A₀(1 + βΔT)

✓ β → Coefficient of area expansion.

◆ VOLUME EXPANSION
✓ ΔV = γV₀ΔT

✓ γ ≈ 3α

✓ V = V₀(1 + γΔT)

✓ γ → Coefficient of volume expansion.

◆ LIQUID EXPANSION
✓ Liquids → Expand mainly in volume because they do not have a fixed shape.

✓ Liquid heated inside a container → Both the liquid and container expand.

✓ Measured expansion → Gives an apparent coefficient.

✓ Real coefficient:
γr = γa + γc

✓ γr → Real coefficient of liquid.
✓ γa → Apparent coefficient.
✓ γc → Coefficient of the container.

◆ BIMETALLIC STRIP
✓ Bimetallic strip → Consists of two different metals joined together.

✓ Different expansion coefficients → Cause unequal expansion when heated → The strip bends.

◆ APPLICATIONS
Gaps in railway tracks and bridges → Allow thermal expansion.

Liquid thermometers → Use expansion of liquids.

Heating a bottle neck → Can help remove a tight stopper.

Sealed containers → Need space for expansion.

Bimetallic strips → Used in temperature-sensitive devices.

✓ Key idea → Heating generally causes expansion; cooling generally causes contraction.

✓ Amount of expansion → Depends on the material, original size and temperature change.

title: 5.5 PHASE DIAGRAM, TRIPLE POINT AND CRITICAL POINT
notes:
✓ Phase diagram → A graph showing the physical state of a substance under different combinations of temperature and pressure.

◆ MAIN REGIONS
Solid
Liquid
Gas/vapor

✓ Boundaries between regions → Show conditions under which two phases coexist in equilibrium.

◆ TRIPLE POINT
✓ Triple point → The unique combination of temperature and pressure at which solid, liquid and gas phases coexist in equilibrium.

◆ CRITICAL POINT
✓ Critical point → The temperature-pressure point where the liquid and gaseous phases merge into a single phase.

✓ Above the critical temperature → A gas cannot be liquefied simply by increasing pressure.

◆ CRITICAL TEMPERATURE
✓ Critical temperature → The highest temperature at which a substance can be liquefied by pressure.

◆ BOILING POINT & PRESSURE
✓ Boiling → Occurs when the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the surrounding pressure.

✓ Increasing external pressure → Generally increases boiling point.

✓ Decreasing external pressure → Generally decreases boiling point.

◆ WATER & CO₂
✓ Phase diagrams of water and carbon dioxide → Illustrate how pressure and temperature determine their phases, triple points and critical points.

✓ Key idea → Phase diagram → Tells which phase is stable at a given temperature and pressure.

✓ Triple point → Solid + liquid + gas coexist.

✓ Critical point → Liquid and gas become indistinguishable.

title: 5.6 CALORIMETRY
notes:
✓ Calorimetry → Measurement of heat exchanged during physical or chemical processes.

✓ Calorimeter → Used to determine quantities such as specific heat capacity and specific latent heat.

◆ LAW OF CALORIMETRY
✓ For an isolated system:
Heat lost by hot body = Heat gained by cold body

✓ ΣQ = 0

✓ This principle → Is used to determine unknown temperatures, masses, specific heat capacities and latent heats.

◆ MEASURING SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY
✓ Important measurements include:

Mass of the substance.
Heat energy supplied.
Initial temperature.
Final temperature.

✓ Using:
Q = mcΔT

✓ For electrical heating:
Q = Pt

✓ P → Power.
✓ t → Heating time.

◆ MEASURING SPECIFIC LATENT HEAT
✓ Electrical method → Known electrical energy is supplied for a measured time.

✓ Method of mixtures → Substances such as water and ice are mixed and the heat exchange is measured.

✓ For phase change:
Q = mL

◆ PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS
Specific heat capacity of solids/liquids.
Specific latent heat of fusion.
Specific latent heat of vaporization.
Heat exchanged during thermal processes.

✓ Key idea → In an ideal calorimetry experiment, energy is conserved: energy lost by one part of the system equals energy gained by another.
